Create a campaign, its list targeting, its messages and its schedule in one call.

The campaign is created as a draft, or as a scheduled campaign when `scheduledDate` names a future date. Creating a campaign does not send it: use `PUT /campaigns/{campaignId}/enable` or `POST /campaigns/{campaignId}/finish` for that.

Requires the Campaign module and permission to create campaigns.

`POST /campaign` remains available for creating an empty campaign from a name and type alone.

delete.description:
Delete several campaigns in one call. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `campaign_delete_list` action.

The body selects what to delete, in one of three shapes:

- `{"ids": [1, 2]}` — the given campaigns
- `[1, 2]` — a bare array of ids, equivalent to the above
- `{"deleteFirst": 5}` — the oldest N campaigns in the account, where N is between 1 and 10

`ids` and `deleteFirst` are mutually exclusive.

Deletion is not transactional: campaigns are removed one at a time, so a call can partially succeed. `deleted` lists the ids that were removed and `failed` the ids that were not, each with a reason. When nothing at all could be removed the request answers `404`.

Requires permission to delete campaigns, and the account must have the Campaigns module enabled.

deleted.description: IDs of the campaigns that were deleted.

failed.description: Campaigns that could not be deleted.

succeeded.description: `1` when at least one campaign was deleted.

The test is subject to the account's test-send limits and to sender-domain verification. Prefix the address with `+` to send through the regular mail server instead of the test mail server.

Responses are plain text, not JSON: `200` carries `test email sent`, and every caller-fixable failure (over the test limit, unverified sending domain, disallowed recipient, invalid RSS feed) carries `400` with the reason. `500` means the send failed without an attributable reason.

put.description:
Enable a campaign for sending, setting its status to `scheduled` (1).

Only a campaign whose status is `draft` (0) or `disabled` (6) can be enabled. For a one-off campaign this also queues the sending engine, so the campaign sends at its existing scheduled date; for a recurring or RSS campaign the next scheduled date is recalculated from the campaign's recurrence settings when it is re-enabled. The scheduled date itself cannot be set here - use `PUT /api/3/campaigns/{id}/edit`.

This endpoint reports business-rule failures in the response body rather than with an
error status: an unknown campaign, an automation ("series") campaign, a completed campaign and a
transition that is not allowed from the campaign's current status all return `200` with `succeeded`
set to `0`. The `message` text is localized to the account language, so match on `succeeded` rather
than on the message.

Pause a campaign that is currently sending, setting its status to `paused` (3).

Only a campaign whose status is `sending` (2) can be paused. Pausing clears the send date on the campaign's most recent process row, which stops the sending engine from picking it up again; a campaign whose process has already finished everything it was given cannot be paused and returns `succeeded: 0` with `Process not found.`.

This endpoint reports business-rule failures in the response body rather than with an
error status: an unknown campaign, an automation ("series") campaign, a completed campaign and a
transition that is not allowed from the campaign's current status all return `200` with `succeeded`
set to `0`. The `message` text is localized to the account language, so match on `succeeded` rather
than on the message.

Retrieve the revenue attributed to a campaign, one row per currency, plus whether revenue is tracked for it at all.

Attributed revenue is a lifetime figure, so this endpoint takes no date window and no paging. Amounts are integers in the currency's minor unit (for example `129900` for `1,299.00 USD`); v1's preformatted `total_revenue_formatted` string is not carried, so format the amount yourself.

Currencies with no attributed revenue are omitted, so `revenues` is an empty array for a campaign that generated none.

Requires the Campaigns feature and access to the campaign; a campaign the user cannot see is reported as `404` so the endpoint does not disclose which campaign ids exist.

Totals are lifetime by default. Supply `startDate` and `endDate` together to restrict them to a date window; supplying only one of the two, or an `endDate` earlier than the `startDate`, returns `422`.

Only a campaign whose status is `sending` (2) or `paused` (3) can be stopped. Stopping is not reversible through this endpoint: a stopped campaign cannot be resumed or re-enabled. It also finalizes the campaign's sending state - the outstanding process row is removed and the campaign's sent totals are written from the counts recorded so far.

This endpoint reports business-rule failures in the response body rather than with an
error status: an unknown campaign, an automation ("series") campaign, a completed campaign and a
transition that is not allowed from the campaign's current status all return `200` with `succeeded`
set to `0`. The `message` text is localized to the account language, so match on `succeeded` rather
than on the message.

post.description:
Upserts up to 250 contacts in one request, matching each one on its email address: an existing contact with that email is updated, otherwise a contact is created. This is the v3 equivalent of looping over `POST /api/3/contact/sync`, and it is the endpoint to reach for when a v1 integration synced contacts one request at a time.

The work is done in the background. The response is a `202` carrying the id of the process that was created, and the contacts are written after the response is sent, so a contact read back immediately afterwards may not reflect the request yet.

A request holding more than 250 contacts is rejected as a whole and no process is created. Rows are otherwise handled independently: a row that cannot be written (no `email`, a validation failure, a contact the caller cannot access) is logged and skipped without failing the rest of the batch, and the outcome of an individual row is **not** reported back anywhere in the API. Use `POST /api/3/contact/sync` per contact when a request needs to know whether each contact was written.

Requires the `pg_subscriber_add` permission.

contacts.description: The contacts to upsert, at most 250 per request.

email.description: Email address the contact is matched on. A row without an email is skipped.

fields.description: Custom field values for the contact, given as field id and value pairs.

202.description: Accepted. The contacts are written by the background process identified by `process_id`.

422.description: More than 250 contacts were sent, or the account's contact limit would be exceeded. No process is created and no contact is written.

post.description:
Merges one contact into another and deletes the contact that was merged. The destination contact survives and keeps its id; the source contact's lists, tags, automations, deals, notes and activity are moved onto the destination, and the source is then removed.

The merge runs synchronously, so the response means the contacts have already been merged. It cannot be undone.

Where the two contacts hold conflicting information, `resolutionFieldId` and `resolutionAutomationId` name which of the two contacts wins: field values are taken from the contact named by `resolutionFieldId`, and automation membership from the contact named by `resolutionAutomationId`.

Requires the `pg_subscriber_merge` permission.

destination.description: Id of the contact that survives the merge.

resolutionAutomationId.description: Id of the contact whose automation membership wins where both contacts are in the same automation. Must be the `source` or the `destination`.

resolutionFieldId.description: Id of the contact whose field values win where both contacts hold a value. Must be the `source` or the `destination`.

source.description: Id of the contact to merge in. This contact is deleted once the merge completes.

422.description: `source` is missing, or `source` and `destination` are the same contact.

post.description:
Upserts a single contact: the endpoint looks for an existing contact, updates it when one is found, and creates it otherwise. A `contact` array holding more than one resource is rejected.

The lookup runs in this order:

1. **Contact id**, only when the request is sent with `lookupByAcId=true` and `contact.id` is set. An id that resolves to nothing does not fail the request; the lookup carries on with the checks below.
2. **`contact.whatsapp_id`**, when WhatsApp contacts are enabled for the account. If no contact has the WhatsApp id and `contact.email` was sent too, the email is tried as a fallback so a duplicate contact is not created for an email that already exists.
3. **`contact.email`**, when no `contact.whatsapp_id` was sent. An email that matches nothing never falls back to the phone number.
4. **`contact.phone`**, only when no email was sent at all. A phone number that more than one contact has is rejected with `Phone must be unique when there is no email`.

Creating a contact needs the `pg_subscriber_add` permission and updating one needs `pg_subscriber_edit`, so the permission a request needs depends on whether the lookup found a contact. Contacts without an email address require phone-only contacts to be enabled for the account and `contact.allowNullEmail` to be set, and WhatsApp payloads require WhatsApp contacts to be enabled.

`ip4` records the IPv4 address the contact opted in from, on the contact and on the list memberships this call creates. Only IPv4 is accepted.

Each `lists` entry may carry an `sdate` subscribe date and the mail subscribing should send: `sendInstantAutoresponder`, `suppressInstantAutoresponder` and `sendLastCampaign`. An entry only accepts those keys plus `list`, and asking for the autoresponders and their suppression at once is rejected.

`form` attributes the write to a form and inherits that form's behaviour: the lists it subscribes to (on top of the lists named here), its double opt-in confirmation — which leaves a membership it creates unconfirmed until the contact confirms — its actions and its `submit` automation trigger. A form ID that does not exist is rejected.

parameters.description: Look the contact up by `contact.id` before the WhatsApp id, email and phone checks. Defaults to `false`, and the id is ignored unless this is set.
parameters.name: lookupByAcId

account.description:
Link the contact to a CRM account, which is what v1 `contact_add`/`contact_edit` did with `orgname`. Name either the `id` of an existing account or its `name`; naming both, or neither, is a `422`.

A contact belongs to one account, so the account named here replaces the account the contact was linked to before, and it takes precedence over the legacy `organization` and `account_name` fields when they are sent in the same request.

The Accounts feature has to be enabled for the account, the caller needs the `pg_subscriber_edit` permission `POST /api/3/accountContacts` requires, and creating an account additionally needs the `pg_account_add` permission `POST /api/3/accounts` requires. The link is resolved before the contact is written, so a link that cannot be resolved fails the whole request instead of half-applying it.

createIfMissing.description: Create the account when no account has the `name`, through the same service `POST /api/3/accounts` uses, so it fires the same events and webhooks. Only valid together with `name`, and defaults to `false`.

id.description: Id of the account to link the contact to. An id that is not a whole positive number, or that no account has, is a `422`. Cannot be combined with `createIfMissing`.

name.description: Name of the account to link the contact to. Account names are unique, so the contact is linked to the account that already has the name. A name no account has is a `422` unless `createIfMissing` is `true`.

email.description: Email address of the contact to sync

form.description: ID of the form the write is attributed to.

id.description: Id of the contact to sync. Only used when the request is sent with `lookupByAcId=true`, and ignored otherwise.

ip4.description: IPv4 address the contact opted in from, e.g. `192.168.1.1`.

lists.description:
Subscribe the contact to these lists, which is what v1 `contact_add`/`contact_edit`/`contact_sync` did with `p[<listid>]`. Each element names the list and, optionally, the date it subscribes as of and the mail the subscription sends: a contact write subscribes, so the membership status is not the caller's to choose.

Memberships are additive: a list this array does not mention is left as it is, so a contact is never unsubscribed by omission — use `POST /api/3/contactLists` to unsubscribe. A list named here becomes an active membership, including a membership that was unconfirmed or unsubscribed before, which requires the same `pg_subscriber_resubscribe` permission `POST /api/3/contactLists` requires.

Entries naming the same list collapse into one. The array is validated before the contact is written, so a malformed entry, a list that does not exist, a list whose channel the contact does not meet the requirements of, or a missing `pg_subscriber_edit` permission fails the whole request rather than leaving the contact written with part of the memberships applied.

list.description: Id of the list to subscribe the contact to.

sdate.description: Date the contact is subscribed to this list as of, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` or `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to now.

sendInstantAutoresponder.description: Send the list's subscribe autoresponders even when the membership already existed or was unsubscribed.

sendLastCampaign.description: Send the list's last broadcast to the contact even when the list does not send it.

suppressInstantAutoresponder.description: Do not send the list's subscribe autoresponders. Cannot be combined with `sendInstantAutoresponder`.

tags.description: Tag names to attach to the contact in the same request. Values are tag *names*, not tag IDs, and a name that does not exist yet is created automatically as a contact tag. Tagging is additive: tags the contact already has are kept, duplicates are ignored, and sending `tags` never removes a tag — use `DELETE /api/3/contactTags/{id}` for that. The value must be an array; any other type is rejected with `400` and the message `'tags' must be an array`. The attached tags are not echoed in the response, read them back through the contact's `contactTags` link. Attaching a tag fires the usual `contact_tag_added` webhook and starts any automation triggered by a tag being added.

whatsapp_id.description: WhatsApp id of the contact, used as the first identifier after `contact.id`. Requires WhatsApp contacts to be enabled for the account; a payload carrying a WhatsApp id is rejected when the feature is off.

source.description: Optional label for the system the write came from. It is not validated against a fixed list. A non-empty value is carried into the `service` key of the contact webhook payload when the payload does not already carry one, which is how an integration recognises, and skips, the updates it made itself.

useDefaults.description: Accepted for compatibility with v1 `contact_sync`'s `use_defaults`, and defaults to `true` on this endpoint. Required custom fields no longer exist, so the value does not change what the request writes.

delete.description:
Remove a contact from an automation without knowing the id of the `contactAutomation` row that links them, so a caller holding the contact and the automation does not have to look it up first. [Remove a contact from an automation](/reference/delete-a-contactautomation) takes that row id in the path instead.

The contact is identified by `contact_email` or `contact`; when both are sent, `contact_email` wins. Only an active run is removed, and if the contact entered the automation more than once, the most recent active run is the one removed — repeat the call to remove earlier ones.

Requires permission to edit contacts.

parameters.name: automation

parameters.description: Email address of the contact to remove. Required unless `contact` is sent, and takes precedence over it.
parameters.name: contact_email

parameters.description: Id of the contact to remove. Required unless `contact_email` is sent.
parameters.name: contact

post.description:
The contact is named by `contact` (an ID) or by `contact_email`, and the automations by `automation` (one ID) or `automations` (an array of IDs); one of each pair is required.

A request using `automations` responds with a `contactAutomations` collection and a `meta` object holding `succeeded` and `failed` arrays of automation IDs, so an automation the contact is already in, or one with no start step, is reported without failing the request. Every automation is validated before the contact is resolved, so a request naming an unknown or inactive automation returns a `422` and creates no contact. A `400` is returned when neither contact field is given, `contact_email` is not an email address, an automation ID is not a positive integer, or more than 25 automations are named.

automation.description: Automation ID of the automation, to be linked to the contactAutomation

automations.description: IDs of the automations to add the contact to, instead of `automation`. Up to 25 per request.

contact.description: Contact ID of the Contact, to be linked to the contactAutomation

contact_email.description: Email address of the contact to add, instead of `contact`. A contact is created with this address when none exists.

parameters.description:
Filter contacts associated with the tags of these names, as the v1 `contact_list` action did. Pass one name (`filters[tagName]=VIP`) or several (`filters[tagName][]=VIP&filters[tagName][]=Lead`), in which case contacts associated with **all** of the named tags are returned, exactly as repeating `tagid` behaves.

Names are matched case insensitively and resolved to tag ids before the contacts are queried, so a name no tag has is a `400` naming the missing tags rather than an empty result. `filters[tagName]` and `tagid` cannot be combined: a request carrying both is a `400`.
parameters.name: filters[tagName]

parameters.description:
Filter contacts by the value of a custom field, keyed by the id of the field: `filters[fields][3]=Chicago`. Repeat the parameter for several fields (`filters[fields][3]=Chicago&filters[fields][7]=Gold`), in which case a contact has to match **every** field named.

Keys must be custom field ids; a key that is not a positive number, a field id that does not exist, or a value that is not a string or number is a `400`.

Values match on a prefix (`Chi` matches `Chicago`), and on any of the selected values for the multi-value field types (checkbox, multiselect, radio, dropdown, list box). An empty value (`filters[fields][3]=`) matches the contacts that have no value for the field, which includes the contacts that have no row for it at all.
parameters.name: filters[fields][{fieldId}]

parameters.description:
Filter contacts by the contact's hash, the value the v1 `contact_view_hash` action looked up. The hash identifies one contact, so the collection contains that contact or is empty; unlike v1's single contact response, the contact is returned in the standard collection payload, so use `include` to side load lists, field values or tags with it.

The filter is ignored when `search` is also supplied.

post.description:
`ip4` records the IPv4 address the contact opted in from, on the contact and on the list memberships this call creates. Only IPv4 is accepted.

Each `lists` entry may carry an `sdate` subscribe date and the mail subscribing should send: `sendInstantAutoresponder`, `suppressInstantAutoresponder` and `sendLastCampaign`. An entry only accepts those keys plus `list`, and asking for the autoresponders and their suppression at once is rejected.

`form` attributes the write to a form and inherits that form's behaviour: the lists it subscribes to (on top of the lists named here), its double opt-in confirmation — which leaves a membership it creates unconfirmed until the contact confirms — its actions and its `submit` automation trigger. A form ID that does not exist is rejected.

account.description:
Link the contact to a CRM account, which is what v1 `contact_add`/`contact_edit` did with `orgname`. Name either the `id` of an existing account or its `name`; naming both, or neither, is a `422`.

A contact belongs to one account, so the account named here replaces the account the contact was linked to before, and it takes precedence over the legacy `organization` and `account_name` fields when they are sent in the same request.

The Accounts feature has to be enabled for the account, the caller needs the `pg_subscriber_edit` permission `POST /api/3/accountContacts` requires, and creating an account additionally needs the `pg_account_add` permission `POST /api/3/accounts` requires. The link is resolved before the contact is written, so a link that cannot be resolved fails the whole request instead of half-applying it.

createIfMissing.description: Create the account when no account has the `name`, through the same service `POST /api/3/accounts` uses, so it fires the same events and webhooks. Only valid together with `name`, and defaults to `false`.

id.description: Id of the account to link the contact to. An id that is not a whole positive number, or that no account has, is a `422`. Cannot be combined with `createIfMissing`.

name.description: Name of the account to link the contact to. Account names are unique, so the contact is linked to the account that already has the name. A name no account has is a `422` unless `createIfMissing` is `true`.

email.description: Email address of the new contact. Example: 'test@example.com'. This field is required unless a phone number is provided and the account has opted-in to phone only contacts.

fieldValues.description: Contact's custom field values [{field id, value}]

firstName.description: First name of the new contact.

form.description: ID of the form the write is attributed to.

ip4.description: IPv4 address the contact opted in from, e.g. `192.168.1.1`.

lastName.description: Last name of the new contact.

lists.description:
Subscribe the contact to these lists, which is what v1 `contact_add`/`contact_edit`/`contact_sync` did with `p[<listid>]`. Each element names the list and, optionally, the date it subscribes as of and the mail the subscription sends: a contact write subscribes, so the membership status is not the caller's to choose.

Memberships are additive: a list this array does not mention is left as it is, so a contact is never unsubscribed by omission — use `POST /api/3/contactLists` to unsubscribe. A list named here becomes an active membership, including a membership that was unconfirmed or unsubscribed before, which requires the same `pg_subscriber_resubscribe` permission `POST /api/3/contactLists` requires.

Entries naming the same list collapse into one. The array is validated before the contact is written, so a malformed entry, a list that does not exist, a list whose channel the contact does not meet the requirements of, or a missing `pg_subscriber_edit` permission fails the whole request rather than leaving the contact written with part of the memberships applied.

list.description: Id of the list to subscribe the contact to.

sdate.description: Date the contact is subscribed to this list as of, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` or `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to now.

sendInstantAutoresponder.description: Send the list's subscribe autoresponders even when the membership already existed or was unsubscribed.

sendLastCampaign.description: Send the list's last broadcast to the contact even when the list does not send it.

suppressInstantAutoresponder.description: Do not send the list's subscribe autoresponders. Cannot be combined with `sendInstantAutoresponder`.

tags.description: Tag names to attach to the contact in the same request. Values are tag *names*, not tag IDs, and a name that does not exist yet is created automatically as a contact tag. Tagging is additive: tags the contact already has are kept, duplicates are ignored, and sending `tags` never removes a tag — use `DELETE /api/3/contactTags/{id}` for that. The value must be an array; any other type is rejected with `400` and the message `'tags' must be an array`. The attached tags are not echoed in the response, read them back through the contact's `contactTags` link. Attaching a tag fires the usual `contact_tag_added` webhook and starts any automation triggered by a tag being added.

delete.description:
Delete a set of contacts, or every contact on the accessible lists. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `contact_delete_list` action.

Send either `ids` or `deleteAll`, never both. `listids` optionally restricts which list relations the delete may touch, as the v1 `listids` parameter did; without it every list the caller can access is used. v1's `_all` sentinel in `ids` is not accepted, use `"deleteAll": true` instead.

The delete is not transactional: contacts are removed one at a time, so a run can partially succeed. `deleted` lists the ids removed and `failed` the ids that were not, each with a reason. When the account's billing-period delete limit stops the run, the response is a `422` with `pastlimit: 1` and `deleted` still lists the contacts removed before the limit was hit.

With `deleteAll`, the id list is a snapshot: a contact that is already gone when its turn comes is skipped rather than reported as a failure.

Requires permission to delete contacts.

deleteAll.description: Set to `true` to delete every contact on the lists the delete applies to. Only `true` is accepted, and it is mutually exclusive with `ids`.

ids.description: Ids of the contacts to delete. Positive integers, and mutually exclusive with `deleteAll`.

listids.description: Restrict the delete to these list relations. Must be a non-empty array of positive integers when given; defaults to every list the caller can access.

deleted.description: Ids of the contacts that were deleted.

failed.description: Contacts that were not deleted, with the reason.

pastlimit.description: Present and `1` only when the billing-period delete limit stopped the run.

succeeded.description: `1` when at least one contact was deleted, `0` otherwise.

delete.description:
Remove a tag from a contact by the tag's name, so a caller that only knows the name does not have to resolve it to a tag id and then to a `contactTag` id first. [Remove a tag from a contact by id](/reference/remove-a-tag-from-a-contact-by-id) takes the tag id in the path, and [Remove a tag from a contact](/reference/remove-a-contacts-tag) takes the id of the `contactTag` association.

The name is trimmed and matched exactly; a name containing a comma or a line break is rejected rather than matched loosely, so a request never removes a tag the caller did not name. Deleted tags are not matched.

Only the association is removed: the tag itself and the contact both remain.

Requires permission to edit contacts and access to the contact.

parameters.description: Id of the contact to remove the tag from
parameters.name: contactId

parameters.description: Name of the tag to remove. Required in this form, and may not contain commas or line breaks.
parameters.name: tag

post.description:
Add up to 100 tags to a contact in one request, by name, by id, or both. This is the batch equivalent of [Create a contact tag](/reference/create-contact-tag), which applies a single tag per call.

`tags` always holds tag names and `tagIds` always holds tag ids; neither array is ever reinterpreted as the other, and at least one of the two must be non-empty. Names that do not exist yet are created unless `createMissing` is `false`; ids are never created. A tag that cannot be resolved fails the whole request, so the contact is never left with part of the requested set.

Tags the contact already has are returned with their original `id` and `cdate` rather than being duplicated, so the request can be repeated safely. The response lists an association for every tag addressed, in the order the request addressed them.

At most 100 tags may be addressed, and a body may reference at most 200 tags in total (a tag may legitimately be referenced both by name and by id).

Requires permission to edit the contact.

parameters.description: id of the contact to tag
parameters.name: contactId

createMissing.description: Whether a tag name that does not exist yet is created. Never applies to `tagIds`.

tagIds.description: Ids of existing tags to apply. Positive integers.

tags.description: Tag names to apply. Trimmed, and may not be empty or contain commas, line breaks or 4-byte characters.

id.description: Id of the association.

Only the association is removed: the tag itself and the contact both remain.

Requires permission to edit contacts and access to the contact.

put.description:
`ip4` records the IPv4 address the contact opted in from, on the contact and on the list memberships this call creates. Only IPv4 is accepted.

Each `lists` entry may carry an `sdate` subscribe date and the mail subscribing should send: `sendInstantAutoresponder`, `suppressInstantAutoresponder` and `sendLastCampaign`. An entry only accepts those keys plus `list`, and asking for the autoresponders and their suppression at once is rejected.

`form` attributes the write to a form and inherits that form's behaviour: the lists it subscribes to (on top of the lists named here), its double opt-in confirmation — which leaves a membership it creates unconfirmed until the contact confirms — its actions and its `submit` automation trigger. A form ID that does not exist is rejected.

account.description:
Link the contact to a CRM account, which is what v1 `contact_add`/`contact_edit` did with `orgname`. Name either the `id` of an existing account or its `name`; naming both, or neither, is a `422`.

A contact belongs to one account, so the account named here replaces the account the contact was linked to before, and it takes precedence over the legacy `organization` and `account_name` fields when they are sent in the same request.

The Accounts feature has to be enabled for the account, the caller needs the `pg_subscriber_edit` permission `POST /api/3/accountContacts` requires, and creating an account additionally needs the `pg_account_add` permission `POST /api/3/accounts` requires. The link is resolved before the contact is written, so a link that cannot be resolved fails the whole request instead of half-applying it.

createIfMissing.description: Create the account when no account has the `name`, through the same service `POST /api/3/accounts` uses, so it fires the same events and webhooks. Only valid together with `name`, and defaults to `false`.

id.description: Id of the account to link the contact to. An id that is not a whole positive number, or that no account has, is a `422`. Cannot be combined with `createIfMissing`.

name.description: Name of the account to link the contact to. Account names are unique, so the contact is linked to the account that already has the name. A name no account has is a `422` unless `createIfMissing` is `true`.

deleted.description: (Deprecated) Please use the the Delete endpoint

form.description: ID of the form the write is attributed to.

ip4.description: IPv4 address the contact opted in from, e.g. `192.168.1.1`.

lists.description:
Subscribe the contact to these lists, which is what v1 `contact_add`/`contact_edit`/`contact_sync` did with `p[<listid>]`. Each element names the list and, optionally, the date it subscribes as of and the mail the subscription sends: a contact write subscribes, so the membership status is not the caller's to choose.

Memberships are additive: a list this array does not mention is left as it is, so a contact is never unsubscribed by omission — use `POST /api/3/contactLists` to unsubscribe. A list named here becomes an active membership, including a membership that was unconfirmed or unsubscribed before, which requires the same `pg_subscriber_resubscribe` permission `POST /api/3/contactLists` requires.

Entries naming the same list collapse into one. The array is validated before the contact is written, so a malformed entry, a list that does not exist, a list whose channel the contact does not meet the requirements of, or a missing `pg_subscriber_edit` permission fails the whole request rather than leaving the contact written with part of the memberships applied.

list.description: Id of the list to subscribe the contact to.

sdate.description: Date the contact is subscribed to this list as of, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` or `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to now.

sendInstantAutoresponder.description: Send the list's subscribe autoresponders even when the membership already existed or was unsubscribed.

sendLastCampaign.description: Send the list's last broadcast to the contact even when the list does not send it.

suppressInstantAutoresponder.description: Do not send the list's subscribe autoresponders. Cannot be combined with `sendInstantAutoresponder`.

tags.description: Tag names to attach to the contact in the same request. Values are tag *names*, not tag IDs, and a name that does not exist yet is created automatically as a contact tag. Tagging is additive: tags the contact already has are kept, duplicates are ignored, and sending `tags` never removes a tag — use `DELETE /api/3/contactTags/{id}` for that. The value must be an array; any other type is rejected with `400` and the message `'tags' must be an array`. The attached tags are not echoed in the response, read them back through the contact's `contactTags` link. Attaching a tag fires the usual `contact_tag_added` webhook and starts any automation triggered by a tag being added.

post.description:
Add a note to the contact named in the path. This is the contact equivalent of [Create a deal note](/reference/create-a-deal-note), and the v3 equivalent of the v1 `contact_note_add` action.

The contact in the path owns the note, so the body never carries the polymorphic `relid`/`reltype` (or `owner`/`ownerType`) pair that [Create a note](/reference/create-a-note) requires: any owner sent in the body is ignored and the path wins.

Requires permission to edit contacts.

parameters.description: Id of the contact to add the note to
parameters.name: id

note.note: Asked to be called back about the newsletter

listId.description:
Id of the list the note is about, which scopes the `subscriber_note` webhook the note fires to the subscriptions of that list, as the v1 `contact_note_add` action did. `0`, `null` and an empty string mean the note is about no particular list, which is the default.

The value only scopes the webhook: it is not stored on the note and it is not returned in the response.

`listId` is not accepted when updating a note; it only scopes the webhook fired when the note is created.

post.description:
Create a new deal

`deal.contact` accepts an email address as well as a contact ID. An address that matches no contact creates one, using `deal.firstName`, `deal.lastName` and `deal.phone` when they are given; those fields are ignored when the contact already exists. Creating the contact requires permission to add contacts (`403` otherwise, and also when the account is at its contact limit), and a non-numeric `contact` that is not a valid email address returns a `422`.

deal.description: This deal is an important deal
deal.title: AC Deal

account.description: Deal’s account id. Required if `deal.contact` is not provided.

contact.description: Deal's primary contact's id. Required if `deal.account` is not provided. May instead be an email address: the deal is associated with the contact holding it, and the contact is created when none exists.

currency.description: Deal's currency in 3-digit ISO format, lowercased.

fields.description: Deal's custom field values `{customFieldId: string, fieldValue: string, fieldCurrency?:string}[]`

customFieldId.description: Field ID, ID of the Custom Field Meta Data

fieldCurrency.description: Required only for the `currency` field type. The three letter currency code for the currency value

fieldValue.description: Updated field value. For `currency` field, this needs to be in cents not dollars (or 100 x Base Unit).

firstName.description: First name used only when `contact` is an email address that creates a contact.

group.description: Deal's pipeline id. Required if `deal.stage` is not provided. If `deal.group` is not provided, the stage's pipeline will be assigned to the deal automatically.

lastName.description: Last name used only when `contact` is an email address that creates a contact.

owner.description: Deal's owner id. Required if pipeline's auto-assign option is disabled.

phone.description: Phone used only when `contact` is an email address that creates a contact.

stage.description: Deal's stage id. Required if `deal.group` is not provided. If `deal.stage` is not provided, the deal will be assigned with the first stage in the pipeline provided in `deal.group`.

title.description: Deal's title.

value.description: Deal's value in cents. (i.e. $456.78 => 45678). Must be greater than or equal to zero.

get.description:
Get event tracking status (enabled or disabled).

Only the status is returned here. The tracked event names are a separate collection, `GET /api/3/eventTrackingEvents`, which is empty while event tracking is disabled - API v2 `tracking/event/list` returned `enabled` and `events` together.

All event tracking endpoints require an account entitled to custom events and return `403` otherwise.

403.description: Forbidden - the account is not entitled to event tracking

put.description:
Enable or disable event tracking.

Send the desired state as a boolean; the response echoes it. This replaces the API v2 `tracking/event/status` action, which took `status=enable|disable` as a form parameter and returned the account `eventkey` when enabling. **The `eventkey` is not returned by v3 and no v3 endpoint exposes it** - event tracking calls are made against the v1 `track/event` endpoint with the key from the account's tracking settings page.

A missing or non-boolean `enabled` attribute returns `422` with an error collection.

enabled.description: Whether event tracking should be enabled

403.description: Forbidden - the account is not entitled to event tracking

422.description: Unprocessable entity - enabled missing or not a boolean

get.description:
List the names of tracked events.

The collection is **empty while event tracking is disabled** rather than an error - check `GET /api/3/eventTracking` before treating an empty list as "no events". Requires an account entitled to custom events.

403.description: Forbidden - the account is not entitled to event tracking

post.description:
Create a new event tracking event (name only).

Event tracking must be enabled before events can be added (`PUT /api/3/eventTracking`); the request returns `403` while it is disabled, and also when the account is not entitled to custom events. The name must be alphanumeric - anything else returns `422`.

This is the v3 equivalent of the API v2 `PUT track/event` action.

422.description: Unprocessable entity - name missing or not alphanumeric

delete.description:
Remove an existing event tracking event (name only).

Returns `200` with an empty body on success. Event tracking must be enabled and the account entitled to custom events (`403` otherwise), the name must not be empty (`400`), and the event must exist (`404`). API v2 `tracking/event/remove` reported all of these as `200` with a `success` flag.

put.description:
Update an existing list.

Only the fields listed below can be changed; any other field sent in the `list` object is ignored. Fields that are omitted keep their current value. `name` cannot contain HTML, and for lists on the `email` channel both `sender_url` (a valid URL) and `sender_reminder` must be present after the update. A list's `channel` cannot be changed after creation.

## Sender address and visibility

The postal sender fields (`sender_name`, `sender_addr1`, `sender_addr2`, `sender_city`, `sender_state`, `sender_zip`, `sender_country`, `sender_phone`) and `private` are updatable, as they are on [`POST /lists`](https://developers.activecampaign.com/reference/create-new-list), so the fields the v1 `list_edit` action wrote can all be written here.

The sender address may be updated in part: when a request carries any of the postal sender fields, the address shown in the footer of the list's campaigns is rebuilt from the list's stored values with the submitted values applied over them, so the fields the request leaves out keep their stored value. A field submitted as an empty string is removed from the address.

delete.description:
Delete a batch of the contacts on a list. Intended for emptying a very large list, which cannot be done in a single call, by repeating this request until it reports that it removed no more contacts.

Only contacts that belong to no other list are removed, so a contact subscribed elsewhere stays in the account. The list itself is not deleted; use `DELETE /lists/{id}` for that.

`limit` is required and caps how many contacts a single call removes.

This endpoint is gated: an account it is not enabled for receives `400` with `You do not have permission to execute this`.

With `structured=0` (the default) the rendered message is returned as one raw MIME string in `result`. With `structured=1` the message is parsed and its headers, parts and attachments are returned as separate members alongside the raw source.

delete.description:
Delete a set of messages, or the oldest messages in the account. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `message_delete_list` action.

Send either `ids` (at most 25) or `deleteFirst` (1 to 10), never both. `deleteFirst` is the bounded replacement for v1's `_all` sentinel, matching [Delete multiple campaigns](/reference/delete-multiple-campaigns); the sentinel itself is not accepted, and neither is a bare array body.

A message a campaign still references cannot be removed without breaking that campaign's history, so it is hidden instead, exactly as v1 did: those ids come back in `hidden`, the ids removed outright in `deleted`, and the ids that were neither in `failed`. With `deleteFirst`, a message that is already gone when its turn comes is skipped rather than reported as a failure.

Messages are deleted under the campaign delete permission.

deleteFirst.description: Delete this many of the oldest messages in the account. Between `1` and `10`, and mutually exclusive with `ids`.

ids.description: Ids of the messages to delete. Positive integers, at most 25, and mutually exclusive with `deleteFirst`.

deleted.description: Ids of the messages that were removed.

failed.description: Messages that were neither removed nor hidden, with the reason.

hidden.description: Ids of the messages that a campaign still references, which were hidden instead of removed.

succeeded.description: `1` when at least one message was deleted or hidden, `0` otherwise.

parameters.description: ID of the message to delete
parameters.name: id

get.description:
Retrieve the report totals of the campaign a message belongs to, with the message applied as the filter. This is the v3 equivalent of calling the v1 `campaign_report_totals` action with only a `messageid`.

As in v1, the message only narrows the totals on a split campaign; elsewhere the whole campaign is reported. The response is the same shape as [Retrieve a campaign report totals](/reference/retrieve-a-campaign-report-totals), and the same date window rules apply: `startDate` and `endDate` must be sent together.

A message that belongs to no campaign is a `404`.

parameters.description: id of the message to report on
parameters.name: messageId

parameters.description: Start of the reporting window, inclusive. One of `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`. A date without a time starts at midnight. Must be sent together with `endDate`.
parameters.name: startDate

parameters.description: End of the reporting window, inclusive. Same formats as `startDate`, and must be sent together with it.
parameters.name: endDate

parameters.description: Set to `false` to exclude opens and clicks attributed to bots. Defaults to `true`.
parameters.name: includeBots

messageId.description: Message the totals are reported for.

revenue.description: Revenue attributed to the campaign, per currency. `null` when the account does not track revenue for it.

status.description: Campaign status. 0 = draft, 1 = scheduled, 2 = sending, 3 = paused, 4 = stopped, 5 = complete, 6 = disabled, 7 = pending review.

subscriberClicks.description: Contacts who clicked at least one link.

totalAmt.description: Contacts the campaign was queued for.

uniqueOpens.description: Contacts who opened the campaign at least once.

uniqueReplies.description: Contacts who replied to the campaign.

unsubscribes.description: Contacts who unsubscribed from the campaign.

updates.description: Contacts who updated their details from the campaign.

verifiedUniqueOpens.description: Unique opens excluding those attributed to bots.

The collection is read-only and currently supports pagination only: `filters[...]` and `orders[...]` are accepted but have no effect, the segment conditions are not included, and the lists a segment is associated with cannot be requested or sideloaded with `include`. get.description:
Retrieve the hosted account and plan information for the account that owns the API key. This is the v3 replacement for the v1 `account_view` action.

Authenticate with your account's API key in the `Api-Token` request header. Only users in the **Admin** group may call this endpoint; requests authenticated as any other user return `403`, as do requests with a missing or invalid `Api-Token`.

> ❗️ Not the same as `/accounts`
>
> This endpoint returns information about **your ActiveCampaign hosted account** (billing plan, contact limits, trial and credit status). It is unrelated to the [`/accounts`](https://developers.activecampaign.com/reference/list-all-accounts) endpoints, which manage CRM accounts (the organizations your contacts belong to).

## Migrating from v1 `account_view`

| v1 (`account_view`) | v3 (`GET /settings/account`) | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `account` | `account` | Unchanged. |
| `email` | `email` | Unchanged. |
| `fname` | `first_name` | Renamed. |
| `lname` | `last_name` | Renamed. |
| `cname` | `cname` | Unchanged. An empty string when no CNAME is applied. |
| `status` | `status` | Unchanged. |
| `subscriber_limit` | `subscriber_limit` | Now an integer instead of a string. |
| — | `subscriber_total` | New. The current number of contacts in the account. |
| `trial` | `trial` | Always present in v3 as a boolean. In v1 the key was omitted entirely for non-trial accounts. |
| `credits` | `credits` | Always present in v3. It is an integer for credit-based plans and `null` for every other plan. In v1 the key was omitted for non credit-based plans. |
| — | `branding` | New. A boolean that is `true` when ActiveCampaign branding links are shown on the account's content. |
| `result_code`, `result_message`, `result_output` | — | Removed. v3 uses HTTP status codes instead of a result envelope. |

The v3 response is a flat JSON object without the v1 result envelope, and the response is never cached (`Cache-Control: private`).

## The v1 `settings_edit` formats

The response also carries the account wide date and time formats (`date_format`, `time_format`, `date_time_format`) the v1 `settings_edit` action wrote, and the settings of the calling user that `POST /settings/account` updates (`phone`, `signature`, `timezone`, `language`). `POST /settings/account` is the v3 replacement for `settings_edit`; the `/configs` endpoints are an internal store of per-user interface preferences and hold none of these settings.

post.description:
Update the settings of the user the API key belongs to, and the account wide date and time formats. This is the v3 replacement for the v1 `settings_edit` action, which wrote nothing but those formats.

The settings of the calling user (`firstName`, `lastName`, `loginEmail`, `timezone`, `language`) are required in every request: this endpoint writes the settings the request carries, so submit the values from [`GET /settings/account`](https://developers.activecampaign.com/reference/retrieve-account-information) for the fields that should keep their value. The three formats are optional, and only an administrator may change them.

A successful request is a `202` reporting whether the update succeeded; it does not return the settings, so read them back with `GET /settings/account`. Invalid input is a `422`.

> ❗️ Not `/configs`
>
> The [`/configs`](https://developers.activecampaign.com/reference/set-config) endpoints are an internal store of per-user interface preferences. They hold none of these settings, and are not the v3 replacement for v1 `settings_edit`.

currentPassword.description: The calling user's current password, required only when `newPassword` is submitted.

dateFormat.description: The account wide date format, returned as `date_format`, as a PHP date format string. This is v1 `settings_edit`'s `dateformat`. Optional, and only an administrator may change it; an empty or unsupported format is a `422`.

dateTimeFormat.description: The account wide combined date and time format, returned as `date_time_format`. This is v1 `settings_edit`'s `datetimeformat`. Optional, administrator only.

firstName.description: The first name of the calling user. Required, and may not contain quotes.

language.description: The language the UI is shown in. Required, and has to be a supported language.

lastName.description: The last name of the calling user. Required, and may not contain double quotes.

loginEmail.description: The email address the calling user signs in with, returned as `email` by `GET /settings/account`. Required, and has to be an address whose domain can receive email. Changing it to an address on an unverified domain sends a verification email and leaves the settings unchanged, reported as a `422`; changing it is not allowed at all when the account signs in through SSO. When it changes, the user's other sessions are signed out.

newPassword.description: A new password for the calling user. Optional; when it is submitted it has to differ from the current password and satisfy the account's password policy.

notificationEmail.description: The address ActiveCampaign sends the calling user's notifications to. Optional, and has to be an address whose domain can receive email.

phoneNumber.description: The phone number of the calling user, returned as `phone`. Optional, and has to be a valid number in international format; a bare national number is a `422`.

signature.description: The email signature of the calling user, which may contain HTML. Optional.

timeFormat.description: The account wide time format, returned as `time_format`. This is v1 `settings_edit`'s `timeformat`. Optional, administrator only.

timezone.description: The timezone of the calling user. Required, and has to be a supported timezone.

get.description:
List every domain on the site tracking whitelist. Each entry is identified by its name; whitelisted domains have no id in this representation.

The collection is **empty when site tracking is disabled** rather than an error, so check `GET /api/3/siteTracking` before treating an empty list as "no domains whitelisted". Filtering, ordering and pagination are not supported.

This is the `whitelist` half of the API v2 `tracking/site/list` response - v3 splits the tracking status (`GET /api/3/siteTracking`) from the whitelist it applies to. For the underlying Prism whitelisting resources, including per-page rules, web personalization and conversations flags, use `GET /api/3/prism/urlWhitelistings` instead.

post.description:
Add a domain to the site tracking whitelist by name. Site tracking must be enabled first (`PUT /api/3/siteTracking`) - adding a domain while it is disabled returns `403`.

A name may begin with `*` to whitelist subdomains (for example `*.example.com`), and must otherwise match `/^\*?[a-zA-Z0-9-.]*[a-zA-Z0-9]$/`: no scheme, no port, no path. Supply the bare domain, not a URL.

The response echoes the submitted object with `201`. This is the v3 equivalent of the API v2 `tracking/whitelist` action, which took a `domain` parameter and answered `{"domain": ..., "success": 1}`; v3 reports the outcome with the status code instead of a `success` flag. Use `POST /api/3/prism/urlWhitelistings` when you need to set the page pattern or the web personalization and conversations flags at the same time.

name.description: The domain to whitelist, optionally prefixed with `*` to include subdomains

422.description: Unprocessable entity - name missing, invalid, or already whitelisted

delete.description:
Remove a domain from the site tracking whitelist by name. The path segment is the domain itself, URL-encoded - no lookup step is needed, unlike `DELETE /api/3/prism/urlWhitelistings/{domain_id}`, which requires the whitelisting id.

Site tracking must be enabled; the request returns `403` while it is disabled, even for a domain that is on the whitelist. A domain that is not whitelisted returns `404` (API v2 `tracking/whitelist/remove` answered `200` with `success: 0`).

Reading or updating a single domain is not supported: `GET` and `PUT` on this path return `405` with `Allow: DELETE`.

parameters.description: The whitelisted domain to remove, URL-encoded (for example `%2A.example.com` for `*.example.com`)

post.description:
Mint a short lived single sign-on token for a user, so an application can drop that user straight into the ActiveCampaign UI without asking them for their password. This is the v3 equivalent of the v1 `singlesignon` action, and the token it returns is produced by the same implementation.

The token is spent by sending the user to `https://{account}.activehosted.com/admin/main.php?_ssot={token}`, from the IP address the token was bound to. Spending a token does not consume it: it stays usable from that address until it expires.

Only a user in the **Admin** group may call this endpoint, and only for a user they may administer; anything else is a `403`, as is minting a token for the account's primary administrator. A user id that does not exist is a `404`.

Minting a token replaces the token this application previously minted for the same user and IP address, and expired tokens are deleted. There is no endpoint that revokes a token: a token stops working when it expires, so keep `duration` as short as the application needs, exactly as in v1.

parameters.description: Id of the user to mint the token for
parameters.name: id

duration.description: How long the token remains valid, in minutes, between 1 and 1440. Defaults to 15 minutes when omitted.

ipAddress.description: The IP address the token may be spent from. Pass the address of the browser the user will arrive from, or `__self` to bind the token to the address this request came from, which is then reported back in the response. A value that is neither a valid IP address nor `__self` is a `422`.

expires.description: When the token stops working, in the account's timezone.

ipAddress.description: The IP address the token is bound to. For `__self` this is the address the request came from, resolved by ActiveCampaign.

token.description: The token, to be spent as `_ssot`.

user.description: Id of the user the token signs in.

post.summary: Create a single sign-on token for a user
